cross_subject: social-studies:ssk-asking-questions (the same habit of asking about the world)
notes: Children look closely at a picture, an object or a short read-aloud on a neutral topic (seeds, snails, rain) and say one "I wonder..." question of their own; the teacher writes each on a class wonder board that later units draw from. Checked alone in kindergarten: each child says a question, not a statement, about the day's topic, recorded on the teacher's checklist. Later grades carry it as they turn wonders into research questions.

How a library works and how to treat it: turning pages with clean hands, putting a book back where it lives, borrowing and returning on a set day. The class book corner stands in where there is no school library. On any day with a device, children learn the stop rule as three pictured words (close, tell, no blame). Teacher note: no library access is assumed; the print path is the class book corner. The adult checks every page a child sees and says what happens if something upsetting appears: the child closes it, tells, and is never blamed. The continuum's K cell names knowing that private information is never shared online; here it is taught in grade 1 (g1-device-stop-rule), the first year a device is used. Checked in kindergarten: the child puts a fetched book back in the bin it lives in and points at the three stop pictures in order.

words: label; spine; story book; fact book
cross_subject: ela:ek-books-and-authors (front cover, title page and the kinds of books)
notes: Children find a book in the class book corner by its spine label (a picture or color sticker for each bin) and sort a small pile into story books and fact books by looking at the cover and a few pages. With help: the teacher names the bin, the child walks to it and brings back a book. Checked in kindergarten: the child brings back a book from a named bin. Carried here; the kinds of sources are checked alone in grade 2. The continuum's K priority skill names labels and ABC order of picture books; here the bins carry picture or color labels, since many class book corners have no ABC shelves, and shelf order comes with g2-catalog-lookup in grade 2. The continuum puts sorting books by fiction and nonfiction in grade 1; here it is done with help on a small pile and checked as story book or fact book, the K cells being that picture books can be true or not true and sorting things and information.

cross_subject: ela:ek-shared-research (recall information to answer a class question); science:sk-needs-places (host task: what an animal needs and where it lives)
notes: The class holds one question (what does a rabbit eat?) while the teacher reads a fact book aloud; children raise a hand when they hear the answer and retell that one fact in their own words. The skill is listening for the part that answers, not every interesting part. With help, on a teacher-chosen book; carried in K to 3.

cross_subject: ela:ek-books-and-authors (naming the author and illustrator and what each does)
notes: Before and after a read-aloud the class says who wrote the words and who made the pictures, and that a person made this book. Children point to the names on the cover. This is the first step of crediting a maker; a credit line written alone comes in grade 2. Telling a found fact (it came from the book's maker) from an idea of one's own, the continuum's K academic-integrity priority skill, is said aloud here.

cross_subject: ela:ek-shared-research (a shared research and writing project)
notes: The class runs the whole cycle once a unit on one wonder: ask (from the board), find (a read-aloud, a picture set, a visit from a staff member), share (each child draws one found fact with a label or dictated sentence and shows it in the circle) and reflect by pointing at the four pictured steps. Children listen to a friend's drawing and say one thing it taught them. Introduces the research cycle model as four pictures.

cross_subject: ela:ek-discussion (taking turns in a conversation); social-studies:ssk-talk-together (talking together in a group)
notes: In a group of three around a picture set, each child takes a turn telling one fact they found while the others listen, then the group says what each friend added ("Sam found that..."). With help, using a talking object. Speaking up with findings is checked alone in grade 3.

cross_subject: ela:e1-shared-research (shared research on a class question); science:s1-parent-offspring (host task: how animal parents help their young)
notes: Before a read-aloud or picture set, each child draws or says one thing they already know about the topic and one thing they wonder, on a two-box know and wonder sheet; after, they mark any "know" that turned out not quite right. Checked alone in grade 1: the child gives a real prior fact about the topic, unprompted. Grade 1 owns it because the move is small and scorable; later grades carry it into research plans.

cross_subject: ela:e1-stories-and-information (the difference between books that tell stories and books that inform)
notes: Given a question (how tall do sunflowers grow?), children choose between a story book and an information book and say why the information book is more likely to answer it, then find the fact-book bin by its label. With help in grade 1; grade 2 names more kinds of source and checks it alone. The continuum's grade 1 priority skill on how the library orders fiction and picture books is met here by the bin labels; shelf order comes with g2-catalog-lookup in grade 2, since many class book corners have no shelves in order.

cross_subject: ela:e1-text-features (text features that help find information)
notes: Children use the cover, the contents page, headings, pictures and labels to find the page in an information book that answers a class question, then show the page to a partner. The skill is searching inside one source for an answer instead of reading from the start. With help, on a teacher-chosen book.

When a child shares a fact, they say where it came from: "I found this in the book (title) by (author)." The teacher models it every share; children copy title and author from the cover onto a sticky note with help. Carried here; the credit line is checked alone in grade 2.

cross_subject: ela:e1-shared-research (a shared research and writing project)
notes: The class runs the research cycle on one question and makes a class information book, one page per child: a labeled drawing and a sentence of a found fact. The book is read aloud to the class and each child says one thing a friend's page taught them. Grade 1 adds the product (a page that answers part of the question) to the kindergarten drawing.

Children give a classmate one star (something the page does well, such as a clear label) and one wish (something to add) using a pictured frame, then the maker chooses whether to use the wish. The skill is advice about the work, kind and specific, not "I like it." With help; checked alone in grade 3.

cross_subject: ela:e1-discussion (building on others' talk in conversations)
notes: Groups of three take pictured jobs (finder, holder, teller) to find one fact in a picture set, swap jobs the next time, and at the end name what each helper added. Grade 1 adds jobs to the kindergarten turn-taking.

On a shared class device, children use only the page the teacher opened and practice the stop rule on pretend cases (a pop-up, a picture that feels wrong): close it, tell the adult, no blame. They also learn never to type their name or school. Teacher note: open search is not used in grade 1; the teacher page says what the adult does if an unsafe result appears and points to the health steps if a child tells you something worrying. The continuum's grade 1 priority skill on a username that protects private information is met here as never typing a name or school; Curio Class sets up no student account, so no username is made.

words: who; what; where; when; why; how
cross_subject: social-studies:ss1-supporting-questions (questions that help answer a bigger question); ela:e2-wh-questions (asking and answering who, what, where, when, why and how)
notes: With the teacher, the class picks a question from the wonder board that a book could answer and pairs write one question-word question each about it, after saying what they already know. The teacher sorts them; children see which ones a book could answer. With help; research questions are written alone in grade 3. Each child first writes an 'I wonder' of their own on a board card, the continuum's grade 2 priority skill on wonders made independently, before the pair writes its question with help.

Children match a question to the kind of source likely to answer it: an information book, a children's encyclopedia, a picture dictionary, a children's magazine, a map or a globe, a person who knows (the school nurse, a gardener), or a page the teacher chose. Checked alone in grade 2: given three new questions, the child picks a fitting kind for each and says why. Owned here; later grades choose among sources (IV.A.3, grade 5). A page the teacher chose stands in for the designated online encyclopedias and databases of the continuum's grade 2 cell, since no device or database is assumed.

Children look up a book by title or author in a printed or invented catalog screen, copy its call label, and find it on the shelf by letter and number order. A practice day uses a shelf of mixed-up books to put in order. On a device they use the stop rule. Checked in grade 2 as the grade's priority skill: the child finds a named book from a printed catalog entry by title or author and shelf order. The continuum lists key-word lookup in K to 2; library leaves key words to grade 3, when children can type or spell them, and owns IV.B.1 at grade 4, where more than one kind of source is searched. Found books go back in shelf order and borrowed books come back on the set day, and any device day follows the school's own device rules (the continuum's grade 2 priority skills on library rules and acceptable computer use).

cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-source-maker (who made a source and why); ela:e2-author-purpose (the main purpose of a text)
notes: For a book or a teacher-chosen invented web page, children name who made it (a writer, a museum, a store) and why: to teach, to tell a story, to sell. Social studies asks who made a source from the past; library asks it of the books and pages students use to find facts, and both are taught in grade 2. The continuum lists naming a site's maker in K to 2; here it is done with help on invented pages, and checked alone with the first lateral check in grade 5, because a K to 2 check of a real site would need open search.

Every product ends with a credit line for each source: title and author, copied correctly from the cover or the page. Checked alone in grade 2: the child writes a correct credit line for a new book. Owned here as the first honest-use move; grades 3 to 12 grow it into a source list, a bibliography and a set citation style. Introduces the citation model (the credit line is its simplest form).

cross_subject: science:s2-water-where (host task: where water is found on Earth)
notes: Children sort found facts, drawn or written on cards, into picture boxes that match the question's parts (where water is, what shape it takes, where it goes). The teacher sets the boxes; children say why a card belongs. With help; notes in boxes they plan themselves come in grade 3. Each card holds a few words or a drawing, never a copied sentence (the continuum's grade 2 priority skill); key-word notes the student plans come in grade 3.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-two-accounts (comparing two accounts of the same thing); ela:e2-compare-texts (comparing two texts on the same topic)
notes: Two books on the same topic give a different fact (how long a turtle lives, how tall a tree grows). Children find the two facts, say what is the same and what differs, and decide to check a third source. Teacher note: K to 5 case sets stay neutral, so the differences are facts about animals, plants, weather and places, never views on politics, religion, identity groups or conflict.

cross_subject: ela:e2-research (a shared research project)
notes: Pairs run the cycle on a class question and make a poster with two found facts, a picture and a credit line, share it with another pair, and say back what the other poster taught them. At the end each child points to the pictured step that went best and the one to do better. Grade 2 adds a pair product and the spoken look-back.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss2-family-interviews (gathering information by asking people)
notes: A research group plans two questions about the class topic (how plants are cared for, what a school job involves) to ask another person (a classmate, a school staff member, or a family member at home), asks them, and brings back the answers; the group then says what each member added. Teacher note: interview rules, APPROACH Sensitive ground 8; a family interview is optional and a staff member can stand in.

words: research question; topic; thick question; thin question
cross_subject: social-studies:ss3-inquiry-questions (compelling and supporting questions); ela:e3-short-research (short research projects)
notes: From a class topic, after a short background read from a source the teacher gives, each student writes three research questions of their own, sorts them into thin (one fact) and thick (needs several sources), and picks one a source could answer. They also sort a set of questions into "I know it", "I need to look it up" and "nobody can look this up". Checked alone in grade 3: three real research questions on a new topic. Owned here; later grades narrow and plan them.

Students pull the key words out of a research question, cross out the small words, search a printed or invented catalog by key word, and try a synonym when nothing comes back, recording each try. Introduces the search plan model: question, key words, where to look, what came back, next try. With the card on the first practice day, without it later. The search ends at the shelf: a printed map of a library's main areas (fiction, nonfiction by subject number, reference) shows which area holds each kind of topic.

words: primary source; secondary source; maker; purpose
cross_subject: social-studies:ss3-primary-secondary (telling primary from secondary sources)
notes: In a teacher-chosen source set, students tell primary sources (a photo, a weather log someone kept, a letter) from secondary ones (a book about it), and for each name the maker and the purpose. Social studies teaches primary and secondary sources the same year on its own cases; library uses the idea to choose sources for a research question. Either order; the second course opens with a retrieval task on the first. When a source states something as plain truth, students check it in a second source from the set before using it, and tell a statement that can be checked from an opinion in a nonfiction account. With help in grade 3.

cross_subject: science:s3-climates (host task: describing climates from information); ela:e3-main-idea (main idea and key details)
notes: Students make notes as key words, not copied sentences, in labeled boxes: one box per research question the student wrote (`g3-research-questions`) or the teacher's boxes, and say why each note goes in its box. With help in grade 3; later grades carry it into notes that answer a question and synthesis. Grade 4 makes its own categories.
Each product ends with a short source list: title, author, year and the kind of source, in the same order every time, from a model. Grade 3 adds the year and the kind to the grade 2 credit line.

cross_subject: ela:e3-speaking-reports (reporting on a topic with facts and details)
notes: Each student makes a product that answers the research question (a short report, a labeled diagram, a fact poster) and uses only facts from their notes, says whether the research answered the question or what is still unanswered, then looks back at the research cycle steps and names one to improve. Checked alone in grade 3: the product answers the question with facts from the notes. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e3-writing-process (strengthening writing with help from peers)
notes: In a gallery walk students read classmates' products and write two notes on one assigned classmate's product (partners assigned so every product gets notes): one thing the work taught them, in their own words, and one specific, kind suggestion tied to the skill card ("add where you found the fact"). Checked alone in grade 3: both notes on a new product, the suggestion about the work and doable. Owns both responding to and advising on others' work.

cross_subject: ela:e3-discussion (collaborative discussion on topics and texts)
notes: In a research team each member finds facts on one subquestion, reports them aloud at the team meeting, and the team recorder writes who added what on a team sheet. Checked alone in grade 3: the teacher observes each student report a finding and name what a teammate added. Owns speaking up with findings and naming what others add.

Students use devices and information responsibly: the stop rule, taking turns on shared devices, never typing a name, school, place or photo into a search or site, keeping a school password to oneself, telling an easily guessed invented password from a harder one on a scenario card (no real password is ever written), and handling books and devices with care. Checked alone in grade 3 on scenario cards: the student says what to do and why. Teacher note: searches use a closed set or a teacher-checked list; the teacher page says what the adult does if an unsafe result appears, with no blame, and points to the health steps if a child discloses harm.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss4-canada-mexico-research (host task: a research project on a neighboring country); ela:e4-research (short research projects on different aspects of a topic)
notes: Students pick an interesting part of a broad topic, write two or three questions about it with a predicted answer, and make a research plan: what they still need to know, which sources they will try and in what order. Checked alone in grade 4: a plan for a new topic whose sources fit its questions. Owned here.

A short free-choice inquiry: each student picks a question of their own from a neutral list or their own wonder (how do bees make honey?), researches it just to learn, names who the sheet is for before choosing its form, and makes a one-page "I found out" sheet with a source list. Checked alone in grade 4: the question is the student's own and the sheet answers it. Teacher note: questions stay on neutral ground in K to 5; the teacher steers a sensitive choice to a nearby neutral one privately.

Students search the catalog, a print or online children's encyclopedia and a teacher-chosen or invented results page for the same question with the same key words, and record what each kind gave. Inside a book they use the contents, index and glossary to reach the part that answers. Checked alone in grade 4: a search plan that uses at least two kinds of source and says what each was good for. Owned here; later grades refine the search.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss4-primary-source (using primary sources); ela:e4-firsthand-secondhand (comparing firsthand and secondhand accounts)
notes: Students compare a primary and a secondary source the teacher chose on the same topic, say what each can tell that the other cannot, and sort invented pages by purpose (inform, persuade, sell, entertain), finding the ad on a page, and check one statement on an invented media page against a second source, marking it supported, contradicted or not settled (the continuum's grade 4 media accuracy cell). Grade 4 adds purpose sorting and the ad to grade 3's kinds.

cross_subject: ela:e4-evidence-inference (referring to details and examples in a text); science:s4-energy-resources (host task: information about energy resources); ela:e4-research (taking notes and sorting them into categories the student makes)
notes: Students read a source with their research question beside them and note only the facts that answer it, in their own words, marking what is opinion as opinion, crossing out "interesting but not an answer" facts. Notes go into categories the student makes and can explain. Checked alone in grade 4: notes on a new text that keep the answers (I.B.1), sorted into the student's own labeled boxes with the plan said (IV.B.4). Owns both.

cross_subject: ela:e4-research (taking notes and giving a list of sources)
notes: Students explain in their own words what honest use means: putting an idea in your own words, using a few exact words in quotation marks with the source, saying where it came from, and why a maker cares; they sort cases into honest and not yet honest, and fix the second kind. Checked alone in grade 4. Teacher note: honest use is taught without shaming; a student who copied is helped to put it in their own words and cite, never named in front of the class.

cross_subject: ela:e4-writing-process (revising with guidance from peers and adults)
notes: Before the feedback round, students check their draft against the teacher's rubric and mark one change it needs (the continuum's grade 4 self-assessment cell). After the feedback round, students choose which advice to use on their research product, make the changes and keep a short change log (advice, what I changed, or why I kept it). Checked alone in grade 4: a revised product with a log that matches the changes. Owned here.

When no source holds the answer, a group works out a new way to find out: a class survey on a neutral question (which of three read-aloud books the class wants to hear again) or an observation plan (birds at a feeder for a week), writes the steps, collects and tallies. Checked alone in grade 4: each student explains the group's plan and why it answers the question. Teacher note: survey rules, APPROACH Sensitive ground 8.

Students plan three open questions to ask a classmate or a school adult how they see the research topic (what they know, what they would want to find out), ask them, listen without arguing, and record the answer. Checked alone in grade 4: the questions are open and the record matches what was said. Teacher note: interview rules, APPROACH Sensitive ground 8.

cross_subject: science:s5-protect-resources (host task: how communities protect resources)
notes: Students judge which questions facts can answer: they sort questions into researchable, opinion, and needs data no one has yet, and rewrite an opinion question as one research can answer ("Which is best?" becomes "Which uses less water?"). Checked alone in grade 5. Owned here; grade 3 sorted known from look-it-up with help.

cross_subject: ela:e5-locate-sources (drawing on print and digital sources to find answers)
notes: Students weigh print, video and online sources for relevance, date and reading level, choose three for their question, and write one line on why each earns its place; one choice may be a group-written online encyclopedia used as a starting map, checked through its references. Checked alone in grade 5. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e5-locate-sources (locating information quickly in print and digital sources)
notes: Starting from a list of key words and synonyms, on an invented results page students change a query when results are poor (narrower, broader, a synonym, an exact phrase), read the source name under each result before clicking, and skip results marked as ads; inside a chosen site, they reach the answering page by its menu (the continuum's grade 5 navigation cell). Grade 5 adds changing the query and click restraint to grade 4's search across kinds.

words: lateral reading; new tab; who is behind it
cross_subject: social-studies:ss5-sourcing-corroboration (sourcing and comparing sources)
notes: Before reading an unfamiliar page closely, students leave it: they search the maker's name in a new tab (or on a printed "what others say" card) and decide who is behind the page and why it was made; then they check one important statement on it against a second supplied source, marked supported, contradicted or not settled (the accuracy half of AASL.IV.B.3). Checked alone in grade 5 on an invented page. Owned here, and introduces the lateral reading model: library is the first to teach leaving the page as a method; social studies sourcing reads the source's own label. Teacher note: invented pages only on practice and check days, the stop rule on any device.

Students keep a search log during an inquiry (terms tried, what came back, what they did next) and at the end look back at it to decide what to do differently on the next search. Checked alone in grade 5: a log with a next-step line that follows from what happened. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e5-research (summarizing information and providing a list of sources)
notes: Students build a bibliography to a model for every source in their product (author, title, date, publisher or site, and the kind of source), print, video and web alike, and explain why an unnamed page is a weak source. Grade 5 adds a set order and web sources to grade 4's source list; one set citation style comes in grade 7.

cross_subject: ela:e5-presenting (reporting on a topic with media for an audience)
notes: Students revise their research product and share it with real people who have a reason to care: a younger class, families at a display, the school office. They pick the form for that audience and answer the audience's questions. Checked alone in grade 5. Owned here.

cross_subject: science:s5-protect-resources (host task: combining information about protecting resources)
notes: A group widens a question by researching together: members split it into subquestions, each brings back findings, and the group pools them into a bigger answer than any one member had, saying how the question grew. Checked alone in grade 5: each student explains what researching with others added to the question. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e5-research (gathering information from several sources)
notes: Students take answer-only notes from three sources on one question, mark where the sources agree and where they differ on a fact, and arrange the notes in an outline or a mind map, chosen for the purpose with a reason, with help. Teacher note: K to 5 case sets stay neutral; differences are factual (a measurement, a date, a count), never views on politics, religion, identity groups or conflict.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss6-research-contribution (host task: researching a contribution); ela:e6-short-research (short research projects)
notes: When a research question is answered, students write the new questions the answer raised and pick one to chase next, building a question chain in the research log. Checked alone in grade 6: a chain of follow-up questions that grow from the findings. Owned here; grades 7 and 8 carry it into longer inquiries.

words: search strategy; quotation marks; snippet; source name
cross_subject: ela:e6-short-research (gathering relevant information from multiple sources)
notes: Students plan a search before typing: key terms and synonyms, an exact phrase in quotation marks, and which kind of source to try first, then choose among results by reading the snippet and the source name. Grade 6 adds planning and choosing among results to grade 5's query changes. The continuum's grade 6 cell on using an online catalog alone is met by grades 2 to 4 (g2-catalog-lookup, g4-search-more-kinds); where a school has a library, the search plan may name its catalog, and no library access is assumed.

cross_subject: ela:e6-short-research (judging the credibility of each source)
notes: Lateral reading taught as the method for judging a source: leave the page, see what other sources say about its maker and its claim, and go upstream to the original of a statistic, quote or photo, then judge whether the information is accurate, fair in its context and fit for the task. Checked alone in grade 6 on invented pages. Owned here, before social studies uses it on news in grade 8. Either order works with ELA's grade 6 credibility work (`e6-short-research`): if ELA's unit comes first, the show-me day reuses its weaker source as the invented case. Teacher note: cases are invented or chosen evenly across views; hoax pages are described or invented, never reproduced.

Students use a group-written online encyclopedia well: read how editing works, check the article's references and edit history (on a dated capture or invented copy), and use it as a map to better sources rather than as the final source. Checked alone in grade 6: the student judges one article's use for a question. Owned here.

words: point of view; stance; word choice; left out
cross_subject: ela:e6-author-purpose (an author's point of view or purpose)
notes: Students spot the point of view a source takes (word choice, what is left out, who paid for it) and weigh it before agreeing, writing "I trust this less because..." or "This fits because...". Checked alone in grade 6. Owned here. Teacher note: cases are invented or chosen evenly across views, on topics like school schedules or products, not current partisan questions.

words: paraphrase; quotation; quotation marks; page number
cross_subject: ela:e6-short-research (quoting or paraphrasing while avoiding plagiarism)
notes: Students make note cards that keep paraphrase, quotation (in marks, word for word) and their own thinking apart, each with the source and page, and fix cases where a sentence was copied without marks. Teacher note: honest use without shaming; a copied passage is fixed with the student privately.

A research team picks a fitting way to talk and share its files (a school-provided shared document, a folder, a notebook passed around) and builds an idea together that no member had alone, recording on a team sheet where each part came from. Checked alone in grade 6: the team's sharing plan (which tool, why it fits, who holds what), scored on use over the unit (III.B.1), and each student explaining the team's new idea and where its parts came from (III.A.2). Owns both. Teacher note: only school-provided tools; no student shares personal contact details.

cross_subject: science:s5-design-test (testing and improving a design)
notes: Students choose what to make from their research (a model, a museum label set, a short recorded explainer, a map) and keep going through trial and error, recording each version and what they changed. Checked alone in grade 6: a version log that shows changes made from trying. Owned here; this is the made product of a research unit. It uses the try-and-improve habit from science's grade 5 design cycle (`s5-design-test`), without its criteria, constraints or fair tests, which stay in science.

cross_subject: ela:e7-author-position (how an author distinguishes their position from others)
notes: Students compare how three or more sources with different views treat one question in a table: the claim, the evidence, the maker, and what each leaves out, then say what a careful reader concludes. Checked alone in grade 7. Owned here. Teacher note: cases are invented or chosen evenly across views; a school may swap a case and keep the id met.

words: claim; source; discussion; "where did that come from?"
cross_subject: ela:e7-collab-discussion (discussion drawing on preparation and evidence)
notes: In a research discussion every claim points to a source ("my source, a ... report, says..."), and students challenge a claim by asking where it came from, not by arguing louder. Checked alone in grade 7: the teacher scores each student's sourced contributions on the record sheet. Owned here.

Students use filters (date, kind of source), a reference work for background before the open web, and a choice rule for which three results to open. Grade 7 adds filters and reference works to grade 6's search plan. Students also use a site's own menus and search box to find the page inside it, and follow a subject heading or category label on a catalog or reference record to related items (the continuum's grade 7 navigation cell and grade 8 subject-heading cell; grade 10 deepens subject terms in databases).

Lateral reading on harder invented cases: a photo with its context lost, a statistic quoted without a source, and machine-made text or images (invented or a dated capture), checked the same way as any source (who made it, what it cites, what others say). Grade 7 adds images and machine-made content to grade 6. Teacher note: no claim that any tool is reliable or unreliable; the check is the same for every source. A post or forwarded claim is shared only after it is checked, and students say why they would or would not pass it on (the continuum's grade 7 cell on not spreading misinformation).

cross_subject: ela:e7-research-questions (following a standard format for citation)
notes: Students cite every source, print, video, image and web, in one set style in a works-cited list and point to it in the text. ELA teaches the format for writing the same year; library applies it across media and to the research product. If ELA's citation format is not yet taught, the show-me day teaches it from the model; ELA's day then retrieves it.

Students add to a class group-written page (in a closed class tool or on a paper wall), writing a section with its sources, crediting others' edits they build on, and reading the history of changes. Checked alone in grade 7: a contribution with sources and credit. Owned here. Teacher note: class space only, no public site, no names beyond first names or initials.

cross_subject: ela:e7-revise-purpose-audience (revising with guidance from peers)
notes: Students ask readers for comments on named parts of their research product, answer each comment in a response log (keep, change, or why not), and use critical comments to improve the product. Checked alone in grade 7: a response log that answers every comment (III.C.1), and at least one change made from a critical comment, with what changed and why (V.D.3). The check scores the use of criticism, never a student's mood. Owns both.

cross_subject: science:s7-human-impact-design (host task: designing a way to reduce a human impact)
notes: A group uses its research findings to come up with fresh answers to a shared, neutral school problem (cafeteria food waste, a noisy hallway), listing ideas before judging them and tying each kept idea to a finding. Checked alone in grade 7: each student names an idea and the finding behind it. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e8-conflicting-viewpoints (how an author responds to conflicting viewpoints)
notes: Students plan searches on purpose to gather sources that see the question differently (an expert body, people affected, a critic) and record in the search plan which view each source brings. Checked alone in grade 8. Owned here. Teacher note: questions are invented or chosen evenly across views.

cross_subject: social-studies:ss8-news-literacy (news and media literacy)
notes: Students apply lateral reading to news items alongside the social studies news unit: tell a report from an opinion piece, check the outlet laterally, and trace a claim upstream. Library taught the method in grades 5 to 7; social studies uses it on news the same year. Either order; the second course opens with a retrieval task on the first. Teacher note: news cases are invented or chosen evenly across views; a school may swap a case. Cases include a news report, an opinion piece, a blog post and a viral video (described or an invented still), each checked by the same method (the continuum's grade 8 cell on methods by kind of source).

With classmates, students compare what several group-written sites say on one question, list the differences, and trace each difference back to the references behind it. Checked alone in grade 8. Owned here.

words: copyright; fair use; permission; public domain
cross_subject: ela:e8-self-generated-research (citing sources in a research project)
notes: Students learn the basics of copyright and fair use: a work is protected from the moment it is made; fair use weighs four questions (why the work is used, what kind of work it is, how much is used, and whether the use takes the place of the original), and giving credit alone does not make a use fair. For invented cases (an image, a clip, a quote in their product) students say which way each question leans and pick the safer path: a public domain or openly licensed work, a smaller part, a link to the work instead of a copy, or asking permission. Checked alone in grade 8: the four questions applied to a new case and a safer path chosen. Owned here. Teacher note: general guidance, never legal advice; students weigh the questions and never rule a use permitted or lawful (APPROACH Sensitive ground 6).

words: assumption; expect; surprise; change my mind
cross_subject: ela:e8-self-generated-research (research from self-generated questions); science:s8-human-trait-technology (host task: gathering reliable information on a technology)
notes: Before searching, students write what they expect to find; during research they mark each finding that tests that belief and say what they now think and why. Checked alone in grade 8: an expectation, the evidence against it, and an honest update. Owned here. Students also say how their own first view shaped what they looked for and trusted (the continuum's grade 8 cell on one's own point of view; the fuller where-I-start note is grade 10, g10-own-lens).

cross_subject: ela:e8-collab-discussion (discussion with diverse partners)
notes: Students work in mixed teams on a question where they see things differently, and link with another class (through a teacher-run exchange) to trade findings and build on what each class already knows. Teams are mixed by each student's first answer to the question, written before research, never by background. Where no partner class exists, the exchange is with another section, another grade, or a findings set left by an earlier class. Checked alone in grade 8: each student shows one change a teammate's different view made (II.B.1) and one change the other class's findings made (III.B.2). Owned here. Teacher note: exchanges run through the teachers; no student shares contact details.

cross_subject: ela:e8-present-reasoning (presenting findings with sound reasoning)
notes: The 6 to 8 course ends with a full research product shared with a real audience (a younger class, families, a school group), with comments asked for and answered in a response log. Grade 8 runs the whole cycle with the least help in the band. Before the search plan, students sort their research questions by the kind of information each asks for (overview, specific detail, cause and effect, comparison), the continuum's grade 8 question cell.

cross_subject: ela:e9-w-short-research (short and sustained research projects)
notes: Students design a research question narrow enough to answer and open enough to matter, and stay with it over several weeks and several rounds of searching, logging how the question shifts. Checked alone in grade 9. Owned here. Grade 9 works inside a topic the teacher sets; grade 10 sets its own topic.

words: database; operator; AND; OR; NOT; filter
notes: Students search a database (a free public library or open-access one, named generically, or an invented one on the print path) with operators (AND, OR, NOT, exact phrase) and filters by date and kind, and compare it with the open web for the same question. Grade 9 learns the operators and filters; grade 10 adds subject terms and following references. Teacher note: no paid database or library access is assumed. Truncation is one of the operators.

cross_subject: social-studies:wh1-sources-of-the-past (host task: judging sources of the past)
notes: Lateral reading on hard cases as a fast routine: stop, investigate the source, look for better coverage, trace the claim to its original. Grades 9 and 10 together hold at least 300 working minutes of lateral reading (nine sessions whose main move it is, about 306 working minutes, listed in the 9 to 12 frame), the amount in the one high school field study (six 50-minute lessons), which is background, not evidence the course gets its result. Grade 9 runs the routine with the card on invented cases; grade 10 without it, on machine-made content. Teacher note: cases chosen evenly across views; hoax pages described, never reproduced. The continuum bolds lateral reading for context at 11-12; library teaches the method from grade 5, and grades 11 and 12 return to it.

Students keep an annotated source log for a long research question, with a judgment line and the date each source was last checked, and recheck it as the question shifts, dropping or adding sources with a reason. Checked alone in grade 9. Owned here.

words: copyright; fair use; open license; public domain; remix; permission
notes: Students read the license on a work (all rights reserved, open licenses with their conditions, public domain), share or remix only as it allows, credit as the license asks, and write a polite request for permission when a license does not allow a use. Fair use in depth: the four questions weighed on harder cases (a remix, a parody, a clip inside a video), where reasonable people differ. Checked alone in grade 9. Owned here. Teacher note: general guidance, never legal advice; no claim that a use is lawful. Checked at 9-10 depth (copyright, fair use, permission); the 11-12 bold on open licenses returns in g10-label-own-work and g11-honesty-review.

cross_subject: social-studies:wh1-sources-and-interpretations (comparing interpretations)
notes: In the research product students present more than one side fairly, stating each view at its strongest with its best evidence before giving their own conclusion. Checked alone in grade 9. Owned here. Teacher note: cases are invented or chosen evenly across views.

cross_subject: ela:e9-sl-discussion (collaborative discussion)
notes: A research group writes a short decision memo for a neutral school or community problem in which the choice follows from what the group found, each step citing the member's evidence. Checked alone in grade 9: each student explains how the group's findings changed their own first idea. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e10-w-research (synthesizing multiple sources)
notes: Students build a synthesis matrix (sources down, subquestions across) and a map of how the ideas connect: where sources agree, conflict and build on each other, and where the gap is. Grade 10 sets its own topic and question for the sustained project (grade 9 worked inside a topic the teacher set). Checked alone in grade 10. Owned here.

Before a research unit students write a short "where I start" note on how what they have read, where they live and what they care about may shape how they read the topic, and after it say whether that happened. Checked alone in grade 10. Owned here. Teacher note: no student is asked to disclose identity, religion, family or health details; each chooses what to share, and the note may stay private to the teacher.

cross_subject: ela:e10-sl-seminar (seminar discussion with diverse views)
notes: Students bring views not yet heard into their research on purpose (a source or interview from a missing perspective) and take part in a seminar where people disagree, adding evidence and listening back. Checked alone in grade 10: a source from a missing perspective added to the source log with a line on why it was missing (III.C.2), and seminar turns on the record sheet that add evidence and say back another view first (II.C.2). Owns both. Teacher note: interview rules, APPROACH Sensitive ground 8; cases chosen evenly across views; ground rules for disagreement are set first.

words: subject term; reference list; cited by; open access
notes: Students use subject terms in a database and follow references both ways (back through a source's reference list, forward to works that cite it), finding open-access copies. Grade 10 adds subject terms and following references to grade 9's operators.

cross_subject: social-studies:wh2-research-argument (host task: a research argument)
notes: Students check machine-made text against its sources: they trace each claim of a machine-made summary to a source and mark claims with no source or a wrong one, without the routine card. The summary is supplied by the teacher as a dated capture or an invented copy; no student uses a tool or needs an account. Grade 10 is the second half of the band's lateral reading time. Teacher note: no claim that any tool is reliable or unreliable.

Students label their own research product so others can credit it: maker (initials or class name in public), date, a chosen license, and full credits for what it uses. Checked alone in grade 10. Owned here. Teacher note: privacy first, no full names or photos on public work. Credits follow the grade 7 citation style (g7-citation-style), embedded at the point of use.

words: method; annotated bibliography; transparent; citation style
cross_subject: social-studies:us1-research-inquiry (host task: a research inquiry)
notes: Students write a method note and annotated bibliography that show how they found, chose and sorted their sources, so a reader could check the work. The annotated bibliography uses one full citation style for every kind of source used, including a report, a data set, an interview and any machine-made text. Checked alone in grade 11 on a short project; grade 12 writes it for the capstone. Owned here.

cross_subject: ela:e11-research (gathering and integrating sources while avoiding plagiarism)
notes: Students look back on a finished project to judge whether it was made honestly and fairly: every quote in its context, credit complete, sources represented fairly, and a disclosure line if a machine-made text tool was used (using one is never required). Checked alone in grade 11. Owned here. Teacher note: taught without shaming; problems are fixed privately; no claim that any tool is reliable or unreliable.

cross_subject: ela:e11-presentation (presenting information for a purpose and audience)
notes: Students publish their research in a form that suits a chosen audience (a one-page brief, an infographic, a recorded talk, an exhibit) and explain the choice. Checked alone in grade 11. Owned here; grade 12 publishes the capstone. Teacher note: published work uses initials or a class name, never a student's full name or photo.

cross_subject: social-studies:us1-research-inquiry (host task: a research inquiry)
notes: Students choose to learn from people whose lives differ from theirs: they plan and hold an interview or read a set of first-person sources from people with different experience of the topic, with consent, and report what changed in their thinking. Checked alone in grade 11. Owned here. Teacher note: interview rules, APPROACH Sensitive ground 8; the difference is in experience of the topic (a job, a place, an age, a way of living with it), never chosen by a group label; no group is treated as one voice.

cross_subject: social-studies:us1-news-reading (news reading)
notes: Students follow a fast-moving invented or dated news case over several days, holding judgment, checking updates and corrections laterally, and rechecking their source log. Grade 11 is the time-pressure case; grade 12 applies the checks to the capstone. Teacher note: cases chosen evenly across views; a school may swap a case. Judge the degree of slant, from a mild lean to propaganda.

words: report; data set; primary data; alert
notes: Students search beyond articles: government and agency reports, data sets and primary data, saving searches to rerun. Grade 11 finds them; grade 12 builds them into a personal system. Contrast a primary data source with a secondary account of it; revisit how results pages order and mark sponsored results (g5-search-revise).

cross_subject: social-studies:us2-research-paper (host task: a research paper); ela:e12-research (sustained research projects)
notes: The capstone: students put a long inquiry to use on a real problem or decision (a school or community choice, a next step after school) and write a recommendation tied to evidence, with the method note and annotated bibliography. The capstone is published for the people the decision affects, in the form grade 11 practiced. Checked alone in grade 12. Owned here. Teacher note: the problem is chosen evenly across views and no partisan stand is required.

words: system; saved search; trusted list; routine
notes: Students set up their own way to find and use information after school: saved searches, a short list of sources they checked laterally, a note system and a habit for checking a claim before sharing it. Checked alone in grade 12: the system run on a new question. Owned here. One next-step search for after school and one goal set from the student's own strengths, both kept private.

Students help others use information safely, honestly and within the law: they teach a younger class or a family member one lateral check, the stop rule or how to credit, with a short guide they made. Checked alone in grade 12. Owned here. Teacher note: visits to younger classes are teacher-arranged; copyright points stay general guidance, never legal advice.

Students map the communities a research topic touches (users, workers, neighbors, future users) and say where they stand among them and what follows for their conclusion. Checked alone in grade 12. Owned here. Teacher note: no student is asked to disclose identity, religion or family details; topics are chosen evenly across views.

Students audit a classmate's capstone source list: check each source laterally, trace two claims upstream and check the citations, then fix their own from the audit they receive. Grade 12 applies the band's checks to finished work.
